text: Consider how changes in production costs might affect suppliers' willingness and ability to produce goods at different prices. Think about what this could mean for the supply curve on a graphical representation of market conditions. Remember that equilibrium price is where demand meets supply; it can change when either shifts, so reflecting on raw material cost impacts will be key here!

Consider how input costs affect supply and what direction would an increase in these costs shift the supply curve on a graph. Think about whether this change increases or decreases the quantity supplied at each price point.

An increase in production costs typically affects suppliers' behavior regarding how much they are willing and able to produce at a given price, not consumers directly or their preferences for quantity demanded. Considering this impact on producers rather than the market demand itself might help you find the right direction of the supply curve shift.
